title: Governed Device Continuity and Destination-Bound Hardware Abstraction
inventive_center: A physical-device continuity process that reconstructs canonical device identity from heterogeneous source-linked observations, preserves unresolved and unsupported states, generates destination-bound non-authorizing packages, requires independently governed destination responses, and retains linked evidence sufficient to reconstruct the path through governance and publication without equating publication or reachability with operational authority.
technical_problem: Existing discovery, fingerprinting, onboarding, hardware-abstraction, inventory, and provenance systems do not jointly preserve source lineage, unresolved states, destination-relative compatibility, explicit withholding of operational authority, independent destination receipts, and reverse reconstruction across source, destination, governance, and publication repositories.
technical_effects: reduces duplicate or conflicting physical-device identities across observation transports
preserves ambiguity and unsupported states instead of forcing classification
separates destination preparation from authority to operate a device
requires destination-side evidence before treating a handoff as accepted
supports reverse reconstruction from public or destination evidence to source observations

implementation_evidence.description: Canonical inventory generation from source-linked device fingerprints.
Destination-bound package generation with constrained response posture.
Independent communication-destination receipt recording observation-only, non-authorizing acceptance.
Independent media-destination receipt recording observation-only, non-authorizing acceptance.
Guardian boundary separating handoff evidence from operator approval, active trust, and behavior authority.
Known public technical disclosure of the governed device-continuity architecture.

notes: Working technical record only. Earlier public disclosures may exist and must be audited. Publication evidence does not establish filing, patentability, inventorship, priority, activation, or operational authority.
